notes: Fifth full sweep (2026-10-22-d, head ba24972, uncommitted false), baseline condition of log-tests: five runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier. Every transcript shows a Read of the input and a Write of the test file followed by elixir -r runs (haiku-1 one Edit, haiku-2 several Edits and side experiments with with_log in its own scratchpad, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 a first Bash heredoc write); no Skill tool call, and reads is empty in all five, as the prompt's last line ("Do not invoke any skills.") requires. Expected reads (now ex_unit.md, since testing.md was renamed) is unmet in every run, as expected for baseline. No session ran mix format.

Rules changed since 3e3581d (git diff 3e3581d -- idiomatic-elixir/): references/testing.md became references/ex_unit.md with its rule headings unchanged. Of the graded rules only "Assert with patterns" changed: its == sentence now reads "The value under test goes on the left of `==` and the expected value on the right, whether it is the call itself or a result bound a line earlier", with a new Instead-of pair. No run puts an expected value on the left of ==, so that sentence decides no verdict; the violations come, as in 2026-10-22-c, from the unchanged sentence "a match that binds the value and an `==` on it afterwards is the shape to replace" and the rule's first example. "Run tests concurrently unless they share global state", "Group tests by function and name them by behaviour", "Replace dependencies at boundaries, through behaviours" and "Capture logs with `capture_log/2`, not a handler" are unchanged and graded to the 2026-10-22-c standard.

Rules outside the list that changed and decide other_violations: "Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call" now says "Unless a call's result is bound to a name, each of its arguments is a name or a short literal ... That holds whether the result is passed on, matched against, nested in another call or discarded." Under that sentence `:ok =\n :logger.add_handler(id, Mod, %{...multi-line...})` (opus-1 lines 42-46, haiku-1 lines 54-58, sonnet-2 lines 32-36), the rule's own Instead-of shape, is reported, and so are haiku-1's discarded and matched charge/3 calls with the options spread over several lines. "Use `do:` for a one-expression body ..." rewrote its clause-consistency sentence; the sentence that decides the reports here is unchanged: "when `mix format` moves it onto a line of its own, the body is too long for `do:`" (opus-1 lines 31-32 and 64, sonnet-2 line 52). SKILL.md gained a "Formatting" bullet under "How to use this skill" and "Before you finish" step 1 now points to it; opus-1 and sonnet-2 fail mix format --check-formatted and are reported under "Before you finish" as in 2026-10-22-c.

"Capture logs with `capture_log/2`, not a handler": 5 of 5 violate, as in 2026-10-22-c. Every run adds a :logger handler that sends each event to the test process and asserts level and metadata on the event maps. opus-1 adds a uniquely named handler (lines 40-46, pid filter at line 31) and silences the console with @moduletag :capture_log (line 37), making no capture call (in 2026-10-22-c its Opus wrapped every call in an option-less capture_log/1). haiku-1 adds a uniquely named handler (lines 52-58, pid filter at line 9) with @moduletag :capture_log (line 46). haiku-2 adds a uniquely named handler (lines 42-43, pid filter at line 26) and wraps every charge/3 call in with_log/1 with no options (lines 51, 59, 68, 79, 87, 100, 108), only to silence the console, discarding the text as _console or not binding it at all. sonnet-1 adds a handler per test (line 33) together with Logger.configure(level: :debug) (line 32) and captures nothing. sonnet-2 adds a uniquely named handler that forwards every process's events (lines 6, 30-36), filters by pid in its drain helper (lines 45-46) and captures nothing. No run passes a :format or :metadata option or asserts on captured text. Calls outside a capture: none in opus-1 and haiku-1 (tag) or haiku-2 (with_log); every charge/3 call in sonnet-1 and sonnet-2, whose runs print 3 and 6 log lines.

To check that the log assertions are not vacuous, each file was run against the five mutants of 2026-10-22-c (success logs at warning, declined logs at info, declined drops amount_cents, request_id metadata removed, unavailable logs at warning instead of error). Every file fails at least one test on every mutant, so the handler approach catches each fault; the rule is broken by shape, not by a weaker test.

"Assert with patterns": 5 of 5 violate with the shape of 2026-10-22-c: bind a log event's metadata with a match (or assert_receive), then compare its fields with ==, where the test already holds the expected values and could put them in the pattern (opus-1 lines 75-77 and 83-84, haiku-1 lines 80-83 and 102-105, haiku-2 lines 63-64, 91-93 and 112-114, sonnet-1 lines 66-68 and 74-76, sonnet-2 lines 72-74 and 84-86). Judgment, as in 2026-10-22-c: the bound value comes from the test's own drain helper, not from charge/3, and is graded under the rule's first example; reading the rule as covering only the call under test would make all five clean. Assertions on charge/3's return value use patterns in every run. haiku-2's `{result, _console} = with_log(...)` followed by `assert {:ok, "ch_test_1"} = result` (lines 50-55) is the exempted destructure plus a pattern, graded clean as before. sonnet-2's `severe = Enum.filter(...)` / `assert severe == []` (lines 61-62) puts the bound value under test on the left, which the rewritten == sentence allows.

"Run tests concurrently unless they share global state": 4 of 5 violate with async: false (opus-1 line 5, haiku-1 line 40, sonnet-1 line 4, sonnet-2 line 10). sonnet-1's is forced by its own global state, Logger.configure (line 32) and a handler with no pid filter (line 27), graded violated as the test-writing standard grades async: false forced by the test's own Process.register. opus-1, haiku-1 and sonnet-2 already isolate their handlers (unique ids and a pid filter in the handler or the drain helper), so nothing forces their async: false; graded violated like 2026-10-22-c's haiku-2. opus-1 says why in line 4 ("# Installs a global :logger handler, so the tests run serially."), which the per-test pid-filtered handler does not require. haiku-2 is clean with async: true (line 34) and a per-test pid-filtered handler; its transcript shows it testing a sync variant and settling on async: true. The Opus tier moves from clean (2026-10-22-c) to violated.

"Group tests by function and name them by behaviour": 0 of 5 violate. opus-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 have no describe block, which the rule does not forbid, so they miss the case's describe check but are graded clean on their test names. haiku-1 names its blocks after conditions ("declined card", "unavailable gateway", "successful charge"); haiku-2 uses "charge/3 when ...". The tersest names are value names, haiku-1 lines 66 and 88 "returns the gateway's error" and haiku-2 line 77 "returns the decline", graded clean as 2026-10-22-c graded "returns the declined error". "Replace dependencies at boundaries, through behaviours" is clean in 5 of 5: every run uses one Payments.Gateway module per outcome, passed through the :gateway option.

Rules outside the list, beyond the changed rules above: haiku-1 reads required metadata keys with meta[:key] (lines 82-83, 104-105). Not reported, as in 2026-10-22-c: the comments above the handler modules (they explain why), handler and gateway modules without @moduledoc false or @impl in an .exs script, haiku-1's meta[:pid] in the handler (line 9), where an event from another source may lack the key, and the 50 ms after-clause in sonnet-1's drain helper (line 47), which waits for time but is not Process.sleep, and the wait rule is outside this case's list.

Tests were run from copies in the scratch folder with elixir -r log-tests-input.ex charger_test.exs on Elixir 1.20.4 (OTP 29), 20 times each with random seeds. Every file passed every time with no compiler warnings: opus-1 3 tests, haiku-1 6, haiku-2 7, sonnet-1 3, sonnet-2 6. mix format --check-formatted passes for haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-1 and fails for opus-1 (line 64) and sonnet-2 (lines 52 and 61), which confirms format_ok in result.json.
